items.name: Social Security Disability (SSDI) & Medicare
items.forWhat: Monthly disability income. ALS is a Compassionate Allowance, so claims are fast-tracked. The 5-month SSDI waiting period is waived for ALS, and Medicare starts when SSDI begins.
items.window: Apply as soon as you are diagnosed and unable to work.
eligibility: ALS diagnosis
Enough work credits (SSI is an option for those without)
youllNeed: Medical records confirming the ALS diagnosis
Work history and earnings
Birth certificate, SSN, bank info for direct deposit
Doctor and clinic contact details
items.howToApply: Apply online at ssa.gov/disability or call 1-800-772-1213. Say 'ALS' so the claim is flagged as a Compassionate Allowance.

items.name: VA Disability Compensation for ALS
items.forWhat: Tax-free monthly compensation, health care, auto and housing grants, and caregiver support. ALS is presumptively service connected and typically rated at 100%.
items.window: Apply any time.
eligibility: Veteran with 90+ days of continuous active service
ALS diagnosis
youllNeed: DD-214 (discharge papers)
ALS diagnosis records
VA Form 21-526EZ
items.howToApply: File on VA.gov or work with an accredited Veterans Service Officer (free).

items.name: Medication Assistance Directory & Discount Card
items.forWhat: A searchable directory of manufacturer patient-assistance programs and copay funds for ALS drugs, plus a free drug discount card.
items.window: Always available.
eligibility: Anyone (each program sets its own rules)
youllNeed: Medication names
Insurance details
items.howToApply: Search by drug or diagnosis on NeedyMeds.

items.name: Communication Device & Voice Banking Help
items.forWhat: Free help with voice banking, choosing a speech-generating device, and securing insurance or grant funding for it.
items.window: Always available.
eligibility: People living with ALS
youllNeed: Contact info
Current speech and access abilities
items.howToApply: Request services on the Bridging Voice website.

items.name: Technology, Equipment & Care Services
items.forWhat: Communication devices, eye-gaze and smart-home technology, power-chair accessories and other equipment not covered by insurance. Also care services and 'Adventure' experiences. Team Gleason Adventures (trips within the US for the person with ALS and chosen companions) is listed separately under grants.
items.window: Rolling. No deadlines are posted.
eligibility: Living with ALS
Read Team Gleason's FAQ and pre-application notes first
youllNeed: Description of the equipment or service you need
Information about what insurance has or hasn't covered
Contact information for you or your caregiver
items.howToApply: Use the online application on Team Gleason's 'Need Assistance?' page and choose the service you need.

items.name: Support for Children & Young Adults (camps, scholarships)
items.forWhat: Free camps, programs and scholarships for children and young adults who have or had a loved one with ALS.
items.window: Program and scholarship dates change each year. Check the site.
eligibility: Children and young adults with a parent or loved one with ALS
youllNeed: Application for the specific camp or scholarship
items.howToApply: Visit Hope Loves Company for current programs.

items.name: Medicare (starts with SSDI for ALS)
items.forWhat: For people with ALS, Medicare coverage begins the same month SSDI benefits start, with no 24-month wait. It covers clinic visits, many tests, durable medical equipment like wheelchairs and BiPAP, and hospice.
items.window: Automatic once SSDI is approved.
eligibility: Approved for SSDI with an ALS diagnosis
youllNeed: SSDI approval
Choose Part D drug coverage and consider a Medigap or Advantage plan
items.howToApply: Enrollment follows SSDI. Ask your clinic social worker or the ALS Association Insurance & Benefits Resource Line for plan help.

items.name: Insurance & Benefits Resource Line
items.org: The ALS Association with Patient Advocate Foundation
items.forWhat: Free one-on-one case management for insurance denials, Medicare and Medicaid questions, disability applications and other benefits.
items.window: Available any time.
eligibility: People living with ALS and their families
youllNeed: Insurance cards and any denial letters
items.howToApply: Start from the program page on als.org.

items.name: Independence & Mobility Program (equipment loans)
items.forWhat: Education on mobility, independence and communication options, plus a free loan inventory of equipment and devices.
items.window: Available any time.
eligibility: People living with ALS
youllNeed: Conversation with your local care services team
items.howToApply: Ask your local ALS Association care services team.

items.name: Virtual Home Assessment
items.forWhat: A virtual walk-through of your home that recommends safety changes and modifications.
items.window: By referral.
eligibility: People living with ALS
youllNeed: Referral from local care services staff
items.howToApply: Ask your local care services team for a referral.

items.name: Ramp Reutilization Loan Program
items.forWhat: Lends temporary, reusable steel ramps for home access, with financial and consulting help.
items.window: Available any time.
eligibility: Living with ALS in a participating area
youllNeed: Home access details
Conversation with the care team
items.howToApply: Contact your ALS Association care team.

items.name: Equipment Loans (Ricky P. Sweat program) & Sally Panfel In-Home Care and Respite
items.forWhat: Free care services for Georgians living with ALS: the Ricky P. Sweat ALS Equipment Loan & Assistive Technology Program lends durable medical equipment and communication devices, and the Sally Panfel In-Home Care & Respite Program pays for short-term in-home custodial care, up to 18 hours a week for a limited time (no more than six months), while a family arranges longer-term care, plus respite stays of 24 to 72 hours for emergencies or caregiver burnout. Eligibility is decided through a needs assessment; people on Medicare home health, with long-term-care insurance that covers care, or living in a facility generally don't qualify for the in-home program.
items.window: Available any time.
eligibility: Georgians living with ALS
youllNeed: Conversation with a Care Services Coordinator
items.howToApply: Call or email Care Services.
items.note: Transportation is a separate program (Paul B. Williams ALS Transportation Program) listed on its own.

items.name: Caregiver Education Certification Course
items.forWhat: Online course on the physical and emotional effects of ALS, safe care, helpful and harmful interventions, and care planning.
items.window: Self-paced.
eligibility: Family and professional caregivers
youllNeed: Online registration
items.howToApply: Sign up from the program page.

items.name: Connect & Serve (volunteer help at home)
items.forWhat: Local volunteers help with one-time or short-term projects such as yard work, seasonal cleanup, painting, outdoor repairs and holiday lights.
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: ALS families in North America registered with Live Like Lou
youllNeed: Live Like Lou family registration
items.howToApply: Register to receive support, and you'll be matched with a nearby volunteer.

items.name: Talk to Me, Goose! communication app
items.forWhat: Free access to a text-to-speech app with personal voice cloning, so you can keep communicating in your own voice as speech changes.
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: Live Like Lou registered ALS families in North America
youllNeed: Registration
Tell them iOS or Android, and with or without ElevenLabs
items.howToApply: Register, or if already registered email support@livelikelou.org.

items.name: JourneyMate Support Program (Radicava / Radicava ORS)
items.forWhat: Out-of-Pocket Savings Program (commercially insured patients pay as little as $0 per prescription up to an annual maximum), a free-drug Patient Assistance Program for uninsured patients with income up to 5x the Federal Poverty Level, and Insurance & Access Specialists who help with coverage questions. Veterans can get Radicava ORS at no cost through the VA.
items.amount: As little as $0 copay (commercial); free drug for eligible uninsured
items.window: Ongoing; copay program requires annual re-enrollment.
eligibility: Copay program: age 18+, U.S. resident, commercial prescription coverage (Medicare Part C/D, Medicaid, VA, DoD, TRICARE not eligible)
Patient Assistance Program: ALS diagnosis, Radicava ORS prescription, no insurance, income no more than 5x FPL
youllNeed: Prescription and signed Benefit Investigation and Enrollment Form from your doctor
Insurance information
Income information for the free-drug program
items.howToApply: Have your doctor submit the enrollment form, then call an Insurance & Access Specialist at 844-772-4548 (the online portal was listed as unavailable); copay enrollment form can also be faxed to 888-782-6157.

items.name: Biogen Support Services for QALSODY (tofersen)
items.forWhat: Support coordinators, insurance help, and two separate copay programs: one for the drug and one for administration costs (anesthesia, imaging, surgical procedure or drug administration) for SOD1-ALS patients prescribed QALSODY.
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: U.S. resident prescribed QALSODY with non-government insurance (regardless of income)
Medicare, Medicaid, VA/DoD, TRICARE and other government coverage may not be eligible
Administration copay program excludes residents of MA, MN and RI
youllNeed: Prescription
Insurance information
Copay Reimbursement Form submitted by your provider for administration costs
items.howToApply: Call Biogen Support Services at 877-725-7639; enroll in each copay program separately.

items.name: Nuedexta Co-pay Savings Card and Otsuka Patient Assistance Foundation
items.forWhat: Copay savings card for commercially insured patients taking Nuedexta (for pseudobulbar affect), and a free-drug patient assistance program through the Otsuka Patient Assistance Foundation for uninsured or underinsured patients.
items.amount: As little as $0 per 90-day or $20 per 30-day prescription (commercial); free drug for eligible uninsured/underinsured
items.window: Ongoing; savings card valid until program expiration.
eligibility: Savings card: commercially insured patients
OPAF: uninsured or underinsured, income-based (FPL), FDA-approved diagnosis, U.S. or Puerto Rico resident
youllNeed: Prescription
Insurance information
Income documentation for OPAF
items.howToApply: Get the savings card at nuedexta.com/savings-and-support or call 855-468-3339; apply to OPAF at OtsukaPatientAssistance.com or 855-727-6274.

items.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) Fund
items.forWhat: Copay, coinsurance, deductible, health insurance premium and incidental medical expense assistance for FDA-approved ALS treatments. Note: the program has been listed as on a waitlist; confirm current status before applying.
items.amount: Varies; assistance through end of calendar year, renew annually
items.window: Accepting waitlist requests. Approved patients are covered through December 31 and re-enroll yearly.
eligibility: U.S. or Puerto Rico resident diagnosed with ALS
Meets household income criteria
Has insurance (commercial, Medicare or Medicaid)
youllNeed: Enrollment form
Demographic, insurance and financial information; additional documentation may be requested
items.howToApply: Check fund status and enroll at tafcares.org or call 855-845-3663.

items.name: Mercy Medical Angels
items.forWhat: Free transportation to medical care: volunteer pilot flights (Mid-Atlantic), commercial airfare, ground transportation and gas cards nationwide.
items.window: Ongoing; request before your appointment.
eligibility: Patients with financial need traveling for medical care; see eligibility page at mercymedical.org/patients/eligibility
youllNeed: Appointment details
Departure location
Provider contact information
items.howToApply: Start a travel request at travel.mercymedical.org.

items.name: Air Charity Network (Angel Flight / Mercy Flight member groups)
items.forWhat: Free flights by volunteer pilots to distant medical facilities, specialists and clinical trials for people who cannot afford or physically manage commercial travel. Regional members include Angel Flight Northeast, Angel Flight Central, Angel Flight (OK/TX/AR/MO/KS) and Mercy Flight Southeast.
items.window: Ongoing; non-emergency, time-flexible trips only. Service not guaranteed.
eligibility: Financially distressed or otherwise unable to travel by public transportation
Medically stable enough to fly in a small unpressurized aircraft; see Passenger Qualifications
youllNeed: Appointment information
Physician release may be required by the regional member
items.howToApply: Use the 'Request a Flight' page to find the member organization for your region and submit a request.

items.name: Healthcare Hospitality Network (hospitality house directory)
items.forWhat: Directory of hospitality houses near medical centers that offer lodging to patients and caregivers at little or no cost while traveling for treatment.
items.amount: Free or low cost (set by each house)
items.window: Ongoing; availability varies by house.
eligibility: Patients and caregivers traveling away from home for medical care; each house sets its own policies
youllNeed: Appointment information; some houses require a referral from the hospital
items.howToApply: Search the House Directory at members.hhnetwork.org/locate-a-house and contact the house directly.

items.name: State Assistive Technology (AT Act) Programs
items.org: AT3 Center / Administration for Community Living
items.forWhat: Every state and territory runs a federally funded AT program offering device loans (try before you buy), demonstrations, reused/refurbished equipment, and in many states low-interest financial loans to buy assistive technology, vehicles modifications or home modifications.
items.amount: Free device loans and demos; financial loan terms vary by state
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: People with disabilities of any age in the state; specifics vary by program
youllNeed: Contact your state program; loan programs typically require a credit application
items.howToApply: Find your state's program on the AT3 Center directory and contact it directly.
items.contact: See state listing on the AT3 directory

items.name: Rebuilding Together (local affiliates)
items.forWhat: Local affiliates and volunteers provide home repairs and accessibility modifications for low-income homeowners, including people with disabilities. Services, eligibility and waitlists vary by affiliate.
items.amount: Typically no cost to the homeowner (varies by affiliate)
items.window: Varies by affiliate; many have waitlists.
eligibility: Homeowner meeting the local affiliate's income and need criteria
youllNeed: Proof of homeownership and income (affiliate-specific application)
items.howToApply: Find your local affiliate at rebuildingtogether.org/find-your-local-affiliate and apply through them.

items.name: National Family Caregiver Support Program (NFCSP)
items.org: Administration for Community Living / Area Agencies on Aging
items.forWhat: Through local Area Agencies on Aging: caregiver information and referral, counseling, support groups, training, respite care (in-home, adult day or facility) and limited supplemental services.
items.amount: Free or low cost; respite amounts vary by area
items.window: Ongoing; funding varies by local agency.
eligibility: Family or informal caregivers of adults age 60+
Caregivers of adults of any age with Alzheimer's or related disorders
Older relatives (55+) caring for an adult 18 to 59 with a disability
youllNeed: Contact your Area Agency on Aging for an intake assessment
items.howToApply: Call the Eldercare Locator at 800-677-1116 or visit eldercare.acl.gov to find your Area Agency on Aging.

items.name: ARCH National Respite Locator and State Lifespan Respite Programs
items.forWhat: Searchable locator for respite providers in your area, plus links to state Lifespan Respite programs, some of which offer respite vouchers to family caregivers.
items.amount: Varies; some states offer respite vouchers
items.window: Ongoing; voucher availability depends on state funding.
eligibility: Family caregivers; voucher eligibility set by each state program
youllNeed: Contact your state Lifespan Respite program or coalition
items.howToApply: Use the Respite Locator at archrespite.org and the State Respite Coalition and Lifespan Respite contacts page to find your state's program.

items.name: Well Spouse Association
items.forWhat: Peer support for spouses and partners caring for someone with a chronic illness or disability: 25+ monthly support groups (including phone groups), 24/7 online support, respite events, webinars and an annual conference.
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: Spouse or partner caring for someone with a chronic illness or disability
youllNeed: Membership sign-up
items.howToApply: Join at wellspouse.org or call the office.

items.name: Wish of a Lifetime from AARP
items.forWhat: Grants wishes (personalized experiences such as reunions and trips) to older adults. Minimum age is not stated on the homepage; check the Submit a Wish page.
items.amount: Wish fulfilled at no cost to the recipient
items.window: Ongoing; wishes reviewed as submitted.
eligibility: Older adults; see Submit a Wish page for current age and need criteria
youllNeed: Online wish submission with the person's story
items.howToApply: Submit a wish at wishofalifetime.org.

items.name: VA Aid and Attendance
items.forWhat: A monthly payment added to a VA pension for veterans and survivors who need help with daily activities such as bathing, feeding or dressing, are bedridden, or live in a nursing home.
items.amount: Monthly addition to VA pension; rate varies
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: Already receiving a VA pension
Need another person's help with daily activities, are largely bedridden, in a nursing home, or have severely limited eyesight
Cannot be combined with Housebound benefits
youllNeed: VA Form 21-2680 completed by a medical examiner
VA Form 21-0779 if in a nursing home
items.howToApply: Apply online at VA.gov, mail the forms to the Pension Intake Center (PO Box 5365, Janesville, WI 53547-5365), or visit a VA regional office.

items.name: Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC)
items.forWhat: For a primary family caregiver of an eligible veteran: a monthly stipend, CHAMPVA health insurance if uninsured, mental health counseling, travel benefits, and at least 30 days of respite care per year for the veteran. Secondary caregivers get counseling and travel benefits.
items.amount: Monthly stipend (varies by location and level of care)
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: Veteran with a VA service-connected disability rating of 70% or more (ALS is presumed service-connected)
Needs in-person personal care for at least six continuous months
Caregiver is 18+ and a family member or lives with the veteran
youllNeed: VA Form 10-10CG (do not send medical records)
items.howToApply: Apply online at VA.gov, mail Form 10-10CG to the 10-10CG Evidence Intake Center (PO Box 5154, Janesville, WI 53547-5154), or bring it to your local Caregiver Support Program team.
items.contact: Caregiver Support Line 855-260-3274 (Mon–Fri 8 AM–8 PM ET)

items.name: SMART Home Program (Wisconsin)
items.forWhat: Loans of Amazon Alexa-compatible smart home devices through the Equipment Lending Program so people with ALS can call contacts, control lights and outlets, stream media, manage lists and calendars, and control the TV by voice.
items.window: Ongoing, subject to device availability.
eligibility: People with ALS served by the ALS Association in Wisconsin
youllNeed: Contact the equipment manager
items.howToApply: Contact Michelle Fredrick, PT, Manager of Equipment and Assistive Technology.

items.name: Equipment Loan Program
items.forWhat: No-cost loans of Hoyer lifts, standard/transport/power wheelchairs, electric hospital beds and air mattresses, rollators, AAC devices and Obi robotic self-feeding devices through vendors across Rhode Island.
items.window: Ongoing, subject to availability.
eligibility: Registered with ALS United Rhode Island (open regardless of insurance or immigration status)
PT/OT/SLP evaluation strongly recommended before requesting equipment
youllNeed: Registration
Therapist equipment recommendation (recommended)
items.howToApply: Register, meet with the Care Services Team, then email support@alsunitedri.org about equipment.

items.name: Scott A. Mackler, MD, PhD Assistive Technology Program
items.forWhat: Communication and assistive technology assessments, help with insurance paperwork for devices, loaner equipment for uninsured or hospice patients, virtual home and smart-home assessments, financial assistance for straight stair glides and modular ramping, and referrals to other funding.
items.amount: Free services; equipment loans free for uninsured/hospice patients
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: People living with ALS and caregivers in PA, NJ and DE; loaner equipment for those uninsured or on hospice
youllNeed: Contact the program; evaluations can be arranged through regional ALS clinics
items.howToApply: Call or text Alisa Brownlee or email alisa@alsmidatlantic.org.

items.name: Team Curtis 4 a Cure Transportation Program
items.forWhat: Wheelchair-accessible transportation within Nevada for medical trips and non-medical outings (restaurants, museums, events, movies, family gatherings).
items.window: Ongoing; at least 2 weeks' advance notice required.
eligibility: ALS diagnosis
Transportation needed within Nevada
youllNeed: Trip details at least two weeks ahead
items.howToApply: Contact an ALS of Nevada Care Service Coordinator at 702-790-1578.

items.name: Free In-Home Care and Caregiver Coaching
items.forWhat: Free weekly home care visits by aides and nurses (as staffing and logistics allow), in-home caregiver training, ALS resource guidance, and Joe's Camps for kids and teens, for families in the Charlotte, NC area.
items.window: Ongoing; visits limited by staff availability.
eligibility: Families living with ALS in the foundation's Charlotte-area service region (service area not published; call to confirm)
youllNeed: Client registration form
items.howToApply: Complete the client registration form on the website or call 704-332-1929; staff will follow up to discuss services.

items.name: Equipment Loan and Transportation Programs
items.forWhat: Free loaner durable medical equipment such as power wheelchairs and Hoyer lifts, plus short rides through Coordinated Transportation Solutions and van rentals for longer trips.
items.amount: Free equipment loans; transportation cost not stated
items.window: Ongoing.
eligibility: People living with ALS served by ALS United Connecticut
youllNeed: Contact Care Services
items.howToApply: Email careservices@alsunitedct.org or call (203) 874-5050.

items.name: Do It For The Love
items.forWhat: Live music wish experiences for eligible applicants. This is an experience program rather than unrestricted cash assistance.
items.window: The current process invites new requests to a waitlist. Earlier waitlist applicants through July 3, 2026 have been invited to apply. Medical verification is part of the process. The waitlist form lets applicants flag urgent, time-sensitive circumstances, but expedited handling is not guaranteed.
eligibility: Confirm eligibility and location
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: Easterseals Massachusetts
items.forWhat: Assistive technology services, device loans, and financing programs.
items.window: Financial loans must be repaid; device loans have their own eligibility requirements. Review each program’s terms. An individual’s prior eligibility result does not determine another applicant’s eligibility.
eligibility: Massachusetts
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: Team Hilliard Foundation
items.forWhat: ALS awareness, research, treatment, and family-support mission.
items.window: A direct individual-family grant process was not verified. Contact the organization about its current support pathways.
eligibility: Confirm service area
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: ALS Hope Foundation
items.forWhat: Clinical care, support, education, and research programs for the ALS community.
items.window: A direct individual cash grant was not verified. Explore its care and support services rather than treating this listing as an open grant.
eligibility: Confirm clinic or program coverage
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: Grants & practical services
items.forWhat: Practical services, transportation, advocacy, and community for people living with ALS.
items.window: The official service page describes grants for treatment-related and ongoing expenses in specified counties in Connecticut, New Jersey, and New York. Check the listed counties and contact MAC Angels about current intake and funding. Exceptional out-of-area grants require organizational approval.
eligibility: Lives in the listed counties of Connecticut, New Jersey or New York
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: Susan Mast ALS Foundation
items.forWhat: Respite, equipment, meals, caregiver resources, and support groups.
items.window: Contact the foundation to confirm location coverage and availability of the specific service you need.
eligibility: West Michigan
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: ALS In Wonderland Foundation
items.forWhat: ALS community resources, support gatherings, and an equipment program.
items.window: The equipment studio invites people with ALS to request available items. Some equipment may require a prescription. Contact the foundation to confirm stock, delivery options, and service-area eligibility before making plans.
eligibility: Arkansas focus; confirm coverage
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: The PHAALS Foundation
items.forWhat: Family support through its Hall of Fame, Diamond Dreams, and LEGEND scholarship programs.
items.amount: No current dollar range verified for family support or LEGEND scholarships
items.window: The publisher describes membership-linked support. Confirm current program operation, enrollment, and eligibility before making plans.
eligibility: Confirm eligibility and coverage
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: With Eddie’s Help Inc.
items.forWhat: An organization lead retained from the 2025 grant list.
items.amount: Amount unverified; a current individual grant program has not been confirmed
items.window: Needs verification: The organization's website directs visitors to its Facebook page, but a current individual grant program, eligibility rules, and application process remain unverified. Ask your ALS social worker to help confirm this lead before sharing personal information.
eligibility: Coverage unconfirmed
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: Hope-JG Foundation
items.forWhat: A foundation lead retained from the 2025 grant list.
items.amount: Amount unverified; a current individual grant program has not been confirmed
items.window: Needs verification: I AM ALS lists this organization, but a current grant program, eligibility, and application process were not verified. The link is to that third-party directory entry.
eligibility: Coverage unconfirmed
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: Les Turner: ALS & Money Guide
items.forWhat: An introduction to financial planning, insurance, benefits, and possible assistance.
items.window: Use the guide to prepare questions for your care team or benefits specialist. Reading the guide does not require grant eligibility at the Lois Insolia ALS Clinic.
eligibility: United States · Educational guide
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: Adaptive Impact: Skydiving & paragliding
items.forWhat: A nonprofit helping people with mobility challenges, including ALS, experience adaptive paragliding and skydiving. Team Gleason shares an ALS participant’s experience with both activities.
items.window: Reach out through Adaptive Impact’s Instagram profile to ask about participation, scheduling, accessibility, and any costs or travel support. Its Give Flight page is a fundraiser, not an application. Team Gleason’s adventure program may be another route to planning support; availability is individual.
eligibility: San Diego, California · Confirm participation requirements
youllNeed: Contact the organization for the current application and requirements
items.howToApply: Start from the official program page.

items.name: Tom & Jill Pulley Mental Health and Wellness Program
items.forWhat: Free psychotherapy with the chapter's licensed clinical social worker for people with ALS and family members (processing the diagnosis, physical changes, caregiver stress, planning ahead), plus Patient and Family Grants for Mental Health: supplemental grants that help pay for a specialized outside therapist, such as one who works with children coping with a parent's diagnosis, speaks your language, or specializes in a particular age group or stage of ALS.
items.amount: Free therapy; grant amounts not published
items.window: Ongoing; ask your care coordinator. Grant caps and any intake dates aren't published.
eligibility: People with ALS and their family members in ALS United Greater New York's area: New York City, Long Island, the Lower and Mid-Hudson Valley, and northern and central New Jersey
The chapter's other grants require registration with the chapter; confirm with your coordinator
items.howToApply: Contact your ALS United Greater New York care coordinator (regional coordinators are listed on the Contact Us page) or call 212-619-1400 and ask about the Pulley Mental Health and Wellness Program.
items.verifyNote: Program page live Oct 22, 2026 (published Nov 7, 2025, modified Sep 23, 2026): 'supplemental grants that provide financial assistance for specialized care'; 'contact your caregiver coordinator'. No amounts or dates. Not part of the Patient Grant Program page (respite, Rx copays, DME; one grant per calendar year; Jul 15 and Jan 15 deadlines).

items.name: Paul B. Williams ALS Transportation Program
items.forWhat: Arranges and pays for door-to-door non-emergency rides (wheelchair, stretcher, or ambulatory) to ALS clinic and doctor appointments or social outings, and short accessible-van rentals through partner companies, for Georgians living with ALS. Also offers financial help toward adapting your own van or car (pre-approval required) and a $1,000 van voucher toward buying an accessible van (written request; chosen on need and impact).
items.amount: Free rides and van rentals; $1,000 van voucher and adaptation help by need
items.window: Apply any time; submit each request at least two weeks before the appointment or rental. One application per trip or rental.
eligibility: Person with ALS living in Georgia
A caregiver or companion must ride along and stay with the person on every non-emergency transport
Each trip needs pre-approval and an authorization code from the program coordinator; cancel 48 hours ahead to avoid a fee
Van voucher and adaptation grants are awarded on need and impact
youllNeed: Transportation Program Application (online or PDF): request type, appointment date and time, pick-up and drop-off addresses, mobility equipment used
Name and phone of the adult accompanying you; signatures from both of you
For van adaptation or voucher requests, a written statement with vehicle and cost details
items.howToApply: Complete the online Transportation Program Application at alsgeorgia.org/navigating-als/transportation-program-application/ (or download the PDF) at least two weeks ahead, or call care services at 404-636-9909 to get started.
items.verifyNote: Program page live Oct 22, 2026: 'non-emergency transportation, accessible van rentals, and other transportation resources'; van voucher 'A $1,000 grant'; 'Please allow two weeks for all transportation-related requests'; application: 'A companion is required to ride and remain with the client'. Ride/rental limits and cancellation fee amount not published; a third-party provider delivers the rides. 2024 impact report: 170 rides and van rentals.

items.name: Section 504 Home Repair Loans and Grants
items.forWhat: Federal help for low-income homeowners in eligible rural areas: 1% fixed-rate loans up to $40,000 (20-year term) to repair, improve, or modernize a home or remove health and safety hazards, and grants up to $10,000 (lifetime) for very-low-income homeowners 62 and older to remove health and safety hazards. Loans and grants can be combined up to $50,000. Not ALS-specific, but a family with ALS that meets the income and rural tests can use it for ramps, bathroom changes, and similar fixes. Not ALS-specific, but it can pay for safety and accessibility repairs when a family qualifies.
items.amount: Grants up to $10,000 lifetime (age 62+); loans up to $40,000 at 1%; combined up to $50,000
items.window: Applications accepted year-round (the federal fiscal year runs Oct 1 to Sep 30); approval time depends on funding in your area.
eligibility: Own and live in the home
Home is in an eligible rural area (check the address on the USDA eligibility site)
Household income below the county's low income limit for loans, or very-low limit for grants
Unable to get affordable credit elsewhere
Grants: age 62 or older; the grant must be repaid if the home is sold within 3 years
youllNeed: Uniform Residential Loan Application (Form RD 410-4)
Forms RD 3550-1 and RD 3550-4 and the items listed in Attachment 12-E
Optional prequalification: Forms RD 3550-35 and RD 3550-1 sent to your local office
items.howToApply: Contact your local USDA Rural Development office (found through the program page) or a USDA home loan specialist in your area; they can prequalify you and take the full application.
items.contact: Local Rural Development office (see program page)
items.verifyNote: Page live Oct 22, 2026: 'Maximum loan is $40,000', 'Maximum grant is $10,000', 'combined for up to $50,000'; grants for homeowners 'age 62 or older'; 'repaid if the property is sold in less than 3 years'; applications 'year round through your local RD office'.

items.name: Non-Medical Respite Program
items.forWhat: Free care services for Nevada families: a non-medical respite program that 'gives caregivers a break from caring for their loved one with ALS', help connecting with grants for ALS-related expenses, loans of durable medical equipment and assistive technology, home visits by care services coordinators, and wheelchair-accessible rides through the Team Curtis 4 a Cure Transportation Program. How respite is delivered (agency hours or reimbursement) and any limits are not published.
items.window: Ongoing; call the care services team to enroll and ask what respite support is currently available.
eligibility: Person with ALS, or their caregiver, living anywhere in Nevada ('Our services are available throughout the entire state of Nevada')
Enrolled with ALS of Nevada care services
items.howToApply: Call 702-777-0500 ('Call Us to Get Started'), or contact Susie Twasta, Care Services Manager, 702-790-1578, susie@alsofnevada.org, or Brian Hubert, Care Services Coordinator, 725-293-0099, brian@alsofnevada.org.
items.verifyNote: Care Services page live Oct 22, 2026: headings 'Non-Medical Respite Program' ('gives caregivers a break from caring for their loved one with ALS') and 'Medical Equipment Program'; intro mentions 'grants to help with ALS related expenses'; services 'provided free of charge'. No respite hours, dollar cap, preapproval rule or application form anywhere on the site. The spreadsheet's 'Respite Reimbursement Program' name comes from a third-party directory, not the org's site.

items.name: Home Visits, Equipment Loans and Support
items.forWhat: Free help for people with ALS in Monmouth and Ocean counties, NJ: regular home visits by the foundation's nurse and social worker to assess needs, loans of hospital beds, mattresses, bed tables, wheelchairs, Hoyer lifts, commodes, ramps and walkers, monthly Zoom support groups for patients (first Tuesday) and caregivers (third Tuesday, 6:30-8 pm), and some financial assistance (terms not published).
items.window: Any time; call or email to arrange a home visit or equipment.
eligibility: Person living with ALS in the foundation's local area: it serves as the regional Monmouth and Ocean County, NJ resource group (ask about neighboring counties)
items.howToApply: Call 732-450-2677 or email info@joandancyandpals.org. For a nurse visit contact Pat Schaeffer, RN, 732-239-4724; for the social worker or support groups contact Irene Stanton, LCSW, 609-433-6333, Irene@JoanDancyandPals.org.
items.verifyNote: Services page live Oct 22, 2026: nurse and social worker 'make regular visits to their homes to assess any needs that we can help with'; equipment list quoted; resources page calls the foundation the 'regional Monmouth and Ocean County Resource Group'. Financial assistance appears only on the foundation's own Sinderella's Ball event site ('medical equipment procurement, and financial assistance'); amounts and rules not published.

items.name: Mobility Matters Van Loan
items.forWhat: Lends a wheelchair-accessible van for temporary exclusive use by a person with ALS on Long Island, NY and neighboring areas, for everyday needs like appointments, errands and family trips. Availability depends on what is already on loan and recent donations; terms and conditions apply. Power wheelchair loans are currently unavailable. People outside Long Island can use the chapter's separate nationwide Wheelchair-Accessible Van Rental Assistance Program for short-term rentals.
items.amount: Free (temporary van loan; terms and conditions apply)
items.window: Any time; 'availability varies based on what is currently on loan and our recent donations'.
eligibility: Confirmed ALS diagnosis (physician name and phone required; may be verified)
Person with ALS located on Long Island, NY or neighboring areas
youllNeed: Online application: contact and pALS details, diagnosis date and physician, proposed use and expected weekly use, passenger seats needed, ventilator use, head-restraint needs
items.howToApply: Complete the online Mobility Matters Van Application on the program page (it can be saved and finished later). Questions: the chapter social worker at rfldirector@aol.com or 631-444-1292.
items.verifyNote: Page live Oct 22, 2026: 'temporary exclusive use', 'ONLY AVAILABLE to PALS LOCATED ON LONG ISLAND, NY and neighboring areas', 'only available to people with a confirmed ALS diagnosis', power wheelchairs 'Currently unavailable'; no loan length, cost or insurance terms published. Can be merged with the row-086 ALS Ride For Life record if the site keeps one mobility entry.

items.name: TIGLUTIK Copay Support
items.forWhat: Copay help for TIGLUTIK (riluzole oral suspension) so eligible commercially insured patients pay $0 per filled prescription, up to a maximum savings limit; applied automatically through Anovo Specialty Pharmacy, the only pharmacy that dispenses TIGLUTIK, which also handles insurance paperwork, ships to your home at no charge and manages refills.
items.amount: Eligible patients pay $0 per fill, up to a maximum savings limit
items.window: Ongoing; EDW Pharma can change or end the offer without notice. No separate enrollment window.
eligibility: Prescribed TIGLUTIK for ALS and aged 18 or older
Commercial insurance that covers TIGLUTIK; each fill must be through Anovo pharmacy
Not eligible if covered by Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE or any other federal or state program
Valid only in the USA, including Puerto Rico; no cash value; cannot be combined with other offers
items.howToApply: No separate application: your doctor sends the TIGLUTIK prescription to Anovo Specialty Pharmacy, which verifies your benefits, applies the copay support and calls to confirm home delivery (caller ID shows AnovoRx Group, 901-201-5470). Questions: Anovo/EDW Pharma at 844-763-1198, pharmacists available 24/7. Ask Anovo about options if you are uninsured or on a government plan; none are published.
items.verifyNote: Patient cost page live Oct 22, 2026: 'Eligible patients pay no more than $0 per filled prescription of TIGLUTIK*', 'Maximum savings limit applies; patient out-of-pocket expense may vary', Medicare/Medicaid/TRICARE excluded, 'Valid only in the USA, including Puerto Rico', 'Must be filled at an Anovo pharmacy'. The page's hidden meta description still says '$50 per filled prescription', so confirm the $0 figure with Anovo; the HCP cost page (spreadsheet URL) blocks automated reading; no cap amount or expiration date published.

items.name: Jack Norton Caregiver Respite Program
items.forWhat: Scheduled breaks for the live-in family caregiver of a person with ALS in North or South Dakota. Choose coordinated respite (The ALS Association arranges a paid aide from a partner home care agency) or self-directed respite (the Association reimburses you for a caregiver you hire, who can't be the person's spouse/partner, parent or child). The program FAQ describes weekly respite in 3-4 hour blocks, up to 18 hours a month, not for emergencies and not a replacement for regular care; respite can continue during hospice.
items.amount: Free; up to 18 hours of respite a month (per the program FAQ)
items.window: Apply any time, close to when you are ready to start; allow up to two weeks for care services staff to contact you after you apply.
eligibility: The person with ALS lives in North Dakota or South Dakota
Applicant is the primary caregiver and lives with the person with ALS
Caregivers of veterans may apply, but the FAQ asks that VA home care and respite benefits be used first
youllNeed: Online application (it also serves as a release of information), then a 30-minute phone or Zoom intake with the program manager and, for coordinated respite, an in-home nursing assessment by the agency
items.howToApply: Submit the online application linked from the program page ('APPLY for the Jack Norton Caregiver Respite Program'); questions to respitemn@als.org or 888-672-0484.
items.verifyNote: Program page live Oct 22, 2026: 'The person living with ALS must reside in either North Dakota or South Dakota', coordinated vs self-directed options, no hour cap on the page; the 18 hours/month, 3-4 hour blocks and $40-50/hour agency cost come from the Oct 2023 FAQ PDF, so confirm current limits. Minnesota is covered by the separate Senator Tomassoni Caregiver Support Program (als.org/mn-nd-sd/tomassoni-program), whose 'Grant Application is currently closed' on Oct 22, 2026.

items.name: Life-Sustaining Generator Loan Program
items.forWhat: Lends Ryobi generators to people with ALS in Upstate South Carolina who rely on a ventilator or other electricity-dependent equipment, so life-sustaining equipment keeps running in a power outage. Generators are delivered and picked up again when no longer needed.
items.window: Any time; immediate safety risks get priority.
eligibility: Person with ALS in Upstate South Carolina
Verified medical need, such as dependence on a ventilator or other electricity-dependent equipment
youllNeed: Generator Request Form (choose 'Generator Loan' on the online assistance application)
items.howToApply: Submit the online assistance application at touchedbyals.org/assistance-application and choose Generator Loan, or call (864) 214-6745 / email TouchedByALS@gmail.com.
items.verifyNote: Oct 22, 2026: programs page says the program 'loans Ryobi generators to people with ALS who rely on ventilators or other electricity-dependent equipment', delivered 'promptly' and 'retrieved once no longer needed'; application dropdown includes 'Generator Loan'.
